soundness_flags.label: ass:positive-rational-design
soundness_flags.one_line: “Known finite randomization with positivity” does not standardly require rational atom probabilities; rationality is an extra restriction needed only for the rational-certificate corollary.

soundness_flags.label: ass:positive-rational-design
soundness_flags.one_line: Positivity is already entailed by defining Z as the support of the randomization, so retain it in the support definition or state only the nonredundant rational-data restriction.

soundness_flags.label: ass:complement-invariant-variance
soundness_flags.one_line: A1_K=0 is a proposal-specific complement-symmetry restriction, not a standard HMS condition under the supplied name and citation.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:studentized-coverage / ass:bound-lln
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Consistency of the realized higher-order bound, W-hat_B minus W_B converging in probability to zero, is assumed rather than derived from the finite-table construction.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The studentized coverage and feasible-normality conclusions are conditional on the stated denominator LLN and blockwise conservativeness.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The author version defines design-compatible quadratic forms and their unbiased estimators, gives the positive-definite targeted-objective complete class, and identifies larger bound classes as open. It contains no complement-symmetry condition; this corroborates, but does not override, the inaccessible 2026 primary version.
The paper supplies a general design-based framework for variance bounds and estimation of linear estimators through matrix/spectral methods, supporting its role as a quadratic-framework comparator.
The article derives a sharp variance lower bound for the randomization-based factorial-effect estimator in binary-outcome 2-by-2 factorial experiments.
The work concerns consistent estimation of sharp variance bounds for the difference-in-means estimator under completely randomized experiments.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Applied Statistics 11, 2017 author preprint
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper combines design, exposure mapping, and estimand; develops inverse-probability estimators and randomization-based variance estimators under general interference; and applies them to a school network experiment.
The paper develops finite-population CLTs for randomization-based causal analysis where the finite population is fixed and assignment is the source of randomness.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the rational-design assumption by ordinary positive real-valued finite randomization throughout the complete-class results, and make rational primal/dual certificates a separately stated rational-input corollary.

Retag A1_K=0 as a novel complement-symmetry condition, give an experiment-design interpretation that makes it empirically meaningful, and state the unsymmetric degree-three counter-regime or limitation.

Make the quartic separation the unambiguous headline by adding a short corollary that every published quadratic candidate is contained in the Boolean quadratic comparison class and is therefore strictly dominated on the displayed witness.

For the school OEQ, specify a concrete bounded-width graph parameter and a certificate-size or termination target, so a successful reduction becomes an algorithmic result rather than only an LP implementation exercise.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two mislabeled standard assumptions and remove the redundant positivity premise; retain the field-level all-degree quartic-separation kernel and carry the coverage theorem forward only as its explicitly conditional supporting result.
